sentences.text: Ritesh Singh vs Gayatri Kunwar on 26 September, 2025

Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:28622
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Gajendra Singh
 On The 26th Of September, 2025
 Criminal Revision No. 4665 of 2025
 Ritesh Singh
 Versus
 Gayatri Kunwar
 Appearance:
 Shri Sapnesh Kumar Jain - Advocate for the petitioner 
 Order

This criminal revision under Section 19(4) of the Family Courts Act, 1984 is preferred being aggrieved by the order dated 21.08.2025 passed in MJCR No.424/2024 passed by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Ujjain whereby an amount of Rs.5,000/- has been awarded in favour of the respondent/wife as interim maintenance.
2.

The marriage was solemnized on 10.05.2023 and the application for maintenance was filed on 23.09.2024 alleging the harassment due to unlawful demand of dowry, negligent in maintenance,
inability to maintain themselves and sufficient means of source of income of respondent/husband.
3. The prayer of Rs.50,000/- per month maintenance was made and an application for maintenance was also filed.
4. The respondent/husband has filed the reply and all the allegations were denied.
It was specifically stated that the wife was not willing to marry with him.
Her marriage was solemnized against her will.
He has filed the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28622 2 CRR-4665-2025 petition for restitution of conjugal rights and the family court passed the decree in favour of the Petitioner/husband.

5. Considering the material available on record including the fact that the F.I.R. under Sections 498A, 323, 294, 506 of the IPC and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 has been lodged against the revision petitioner/husband, the learned Family Court has partly allowed the interim maintenance application and awarded maintenance as mentioned in para no.1 of the order.
6. Challenging the amount of maintenance, this revision petition has been preferred by stating that the respondent/wife is earning by doing stitching, embroidery & parlor.

It is also submitted that Ritesh Singh vs Gayatri Kunwar on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62686237/
1 some agricultural land is in the name of respondent/wife whereas revision petitioner/husband is pursuing his B.Tech.

sentences.text: Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7. The affidavit of revision petitioner filed in compliance of Rajnesh Vs. Neha and Another (2021) 2 SCC 324 discloses that he is a student of B.Tech 3 rd year.

entities.text: Rajnesh Vs. Neha and Another (2021) 2 SCC 324
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The decree of conjugal rights is in favour of the petitioner/husband.
No execution has been filed.
The trial Court has recorded the cogent reasons for allowing the application partially.
8. The scope of revision against the order of interim maintenance is very limited.
9. Considering the amount of maintenance, the impugned order does not fall within the limited scope of revision against the interim maintenance.
The scope of revision against the order of interim maintenance is very NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28622 3 CRR-4665-2025 limited.
Hence, this criminal revision is dismissed.

10. Record of the trial Court be remitted back immediately and the Family Court, Ujjain is directed to dispose of the application, as early as possible, preferably within three months from the date of receipt of this order.

The revision petitioner/husband may raise all the objections before the Family Court and the Family Court is directed to pass the order without being prejudiced by the rejection of this criminal revision.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
